results.title: Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm's future in question as LIV Golf fail to confirm stars will stay in league
results.description: Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm's futures are in question after LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil failed to confirm whether the stars will stay in the league. O'Neil spoke to the press after announcing that LIV had secured a new investment package that will help drive the league into its "new era". The league's future has been up in the air after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced in April that it would withdraw its backing at the end of the season. With the new investment, LIV's upcoming season looks to be in a stronger position, but its personnel may not be, as O'Neil did not say if Rahm and DeChambeau will be featuring. TRENDING Stories Videos Your Say When asked about the importance of keeping the pair, he said: "Yeah, it's wonderful. We've been blessed with stars. I define it a little bit differently, and for those of you who have had the privilege and pleasure to travel with us around the world, you get to see it. "But I don't think there was any bigger star on the planet in South Africa than Dean Burmester. And I don't think there was any bigger star on the planet than Cam Smith when we were in Australia. "I think when you have a global game, and you have 57 players from 21 countries, and you're playing in 10 countries on five continents, how you define stars gets really interesting. "So while I have all the time in the world for Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau, I think I'd be remiss in saying they're not only two of the biggest, best golfers on the planet, but I think they're some of the biggest stars in sports, let alone golf." LATEST SPORTS NEWS LIV Golf's future handed major boost as new investment 'signed' and 'approved' Jane Moore mocks Adam Peaty's Christian forgiveness stance amid family rift: 'Big of him!' FIFA President Gianni Infantino 'promises Morocco World Cup final' in return for its support O'Neil continued: "Would certainly love them to come along for the ride and journey because they carry maybe more weight than anybody in the game, and I have a lot of time for that. "I think we have enough support from enough players, and we have such an interesting format and global format, I think we'll do quite well in getting the right stars for this game." DeChambeau appears more set to stay than Rahm after hosting a players' meeting yesterday and has publicly stated his commitment to continue with the league. Meanwhile, Rahm's position appears more tenable after refusing to commit his future to the breakaway league. The Spaniard will have a nine-figure sum outstanding on his contract once this current season comes to an end. In May, he struck a deal to play on the DP World Tour, which paved the way for his return to the European circuit and qualifying for the Ryder Cup. Rahm forked out a fee understood to be approximately $3million (£2.21m) in fines accumulated since 2024. A spokesman for the DP World Tour said: "The DP World Tour and Jon Rahm have come to an agreement on conditional releases to play in conflicting tournaments on LIV Golf during the remainder of its 2026 season. "This involves payment of all outstanding fines accrued from 2024 to date, along with participation in agreed DP World Tour tournaments (outside the Majors) in the remainder of the 2026 season." Rahm won the Masters back in 2023 and is arguably the biggest name on the league's circuit. Our Standards: The GB News Editorial Charter

results.title: Onlookers astonished as GOP governor tells Trump crowd to stop booing dead cop
results.description: The internet was stunned Wednesday after Nevada Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo had to tell a crowd of Trump supporters not to boo a fallen police officer. Lombardo was speaking in Las Vegas touting Trump accounts when he mentioned police officer Austin Abdelnabi, a Marine veteran who died following a shootout with a suspect on Tuesday. "So I know the pastor spoke about Officer Abdelnabi," said Lombardo, who was interrupted by booing. "No. We're not booing him. He's the officer that passed away," Lombardo said. The crowd quieted down as Lombardo said he wanted to offer a moment of silence for Abdelnabi. On social media, critics called out the crowd's reaction to hearing the officer's name and their immediate response. "The booing of what sounds like a foreign (and no doubt in the man's mind, 'Islamic') name really speaks volumes about the mindset of some Trump supporters. Even when Trump is gone, this white Christian nationalist section of US society will still remain," Dr. Steven Buckley, lecturer in Digital Media Sociology at City St. George's at the University of London, wrote on Bluesky. "It’s a Klan Rally. These people only have to hear a name that their lizard brains process as sounding Arabic and hate immediately pours out," Bluesky user Danielle Blake, a political commentator who self-identifies as a "British social Democrat" and has more than 1,500 followers, wrote . "Are they booing because they think he's a Muslim? That'd be really crappy," Amanda Berry, a progressive political commentator and veteran, wrote on X. "Oh my....even their racism is racist," writer and editor Keith Murphy posted on X. Oh my....even their racism is racist.....🤣😂😆 https://t.co/sNjn1qOazC — Keith Murphy (@murphdogg29) August 5, 2026
